quest.name: A Dry Hand in a Wet City

stages.journal: S'Tabi, a Khajiit trader on Soulrest's dock, told me that if I want quiet work I should ask for Tilts-The-Jug inside the house behind him. I'm to speak to her.

Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk, wants to see how I work, and gave me three lockpicks. A dock thief, Keeps-What-Floats, took a Chapter Lookout's necklace of blue jaspers and keeps it in his strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. I'm to bring it back with no harm to him.
I talked Keeps-What-Floats round, and he gave me the key to his strongbox. I'm to take the necklace out of it, under the eaves north-west of the house.
I paid Keeps-What-Floats sixty gold, and he gave me the key to his strongbox. I'm to take the necklace out of it, under the eaves north-west of the house.
I took the necklace of blue jaspers out of Keeps-What-Floats's strongbox. I'm to bring it to Tilts-The-Jug inside the house on Soulrest's dock, behind the door beside S'Tabi.

I gave Tilts-The-Jug the necklace, and since Keeps-What-Floats came to no harm I was paid a hundred gold. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, go down the trapdoor north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water, and speak to Bent-Spine below.

I gave Tilts-The-Jug the necklace, but Keeps-What-Floats is dead, and the Chapter wanted no killing for it, so I was paid nothing. I'm to take the coast ship to Lilmoth, go down the trapdoor north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water, and speak to Bent-Spine below.
I went down through the trapdoor north of Pusbottom to the Night-Reed Chapter under Lilmoth, and Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, took me in as a Lookout.
Tilts-The-Jug, who kept the Night-Reed Chapter's desk at Soulrest, is dead. The Chapter will not take me in now.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence under Lilmoth, is dead. The Chapter will not take me in now.

stages.journal: Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, has work for me now that I am a Lookout. I'm to ask him about it, in the Chapter's inner room under Lilmoth.

A merchant drowned in the deep water north of Pusbottom, and his locked lockbox of pledges lies on the floor. Bent-Spine wants what is in it before three clients on the bank find a diver, and leaves the rest to me; he gave me three lockpicks. I'm to dive to the lockbox, pick its lock and take what is inside.

I went back to Bent-Spine for more lockpicks; he gave me three more and said there would be no others. I'm to dive to the lockbox in the deep water north of Pusbottom, pick its lock and take what is inside.

I opened the drowned merchant's lockbox. In it were a worn bone figurine, a Neesak charm (a green scrying crystal in a new silver mount) and Kothringi glass beads, each claimed by one of the three clients on the bank. I'm to give all three to one client, or sell each to the one who claims it.

Neeta-Haj said the bone figurine was carved for her clutch, but it is older than any clutch of hers. When I said so, she bought it for forty gold, its fair price. I'm to sell Okan-Tei the Neesak charm he claims.

Okan-Tei said the Neesak charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. When I said so, he bought it for ninety gold, its fair price. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the glass beads he claims.
Okan-Tei said the Neesak charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. He haggled, and bought it back for forty-five gold. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the glass beads he claims.

I brought up the drowned merchant's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom and gave all three to Neeta-Haj on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel will not forget it.

I brought up the drowned merchant's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom and gave all three to Okan-Tei on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. Neeta-Haj and Dar-Zeel will not forget it.

I brought up the drowned merchant's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom and gave all three to Dar-Zeel on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. Neeta-Haj and Okan-Tei will not forget it.

Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. He bought them for fifty-five gold, their fair price. Each of the drowned merchant's three clients has bought back the pledge they lied about, and none of them is pleased with me.

Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. He haggled, and bought them back for thirty gold. Each of the drowned merchant's three clients has bought back the pledge they lied about, and none of them is pleased with me.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, is dead, and the job he gave me died with him.
One of the drowned merchant's three clients, Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei or Dar-Zeel, is dead, and the pledges cannot be settled now. The job for Bent-Spine has come to nothing.

lines: Slaughterfish swim in the water just north of my lily pads, and more just south-west. They take the catch off my line. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore just south-south-west, so keep out of the water, dry-foot.
Lilmoth? Follow the shore east a fair way and Lilmoth is there. Keep to the bank and out of the water, dry-foot.
Hereguard Plantation? Follow the path west just until you reach the dead tree. Then follow the path south-west a short way, and Hereguard is there. I buy my bait there.
Ah, you came back, my friend. Sit on the bank and watch the pads with me.
Dry-foot. Keep to the bank and do not splash. The fish are feeding.
Wild leeks grow on the bank a short way east-south-east of here. Take them from the bank and not from my lily pads, dry-foot.
A giant crab lives in the shallows a short way south-south-west, and he is called Old Salty. I will say no more about him to a dry-foot I do not know.
I am Uleesh. I fish the shallows below the walls and sell my catch inside. The rent inside is more than I can get for fish, so I stay out here. Twenty years on the same water now.
Lilmoth Dock, walker. Go north-east a fair way. The burnt-out house stands on the way, and the dock lies past it.
Lilmoth lies north, walker. It is a fair way on foot. We stay clear of its rents.
Walker, my friend, welcome. Sit by the spit. There is always a place here for you.
Walker. You stand at our spit. Say what you want and I will hear it.

This is our village, walker. A few families live on the marsh outside Lilmoth. The cooking spit stands in the middle of the village. From the spit, the carpenter's bench is just south-south-east and a food barrel just east-south-east.
We keep a second hearth just west of this spit, on the west edge of the village. It has food barrels, a cooking pot and a bed. They belong to the families.
Lilmoth has no single ruler. A council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets. I want no seat among them. So it is.
In Lilmoth people take their quarrels to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them, not to a court. We do the same here. The elders speak at this spit.
I am Flaa Heet. I lead the families who live here. I stand at the spit because every quarrel and every catch comes to it in the end.
Tseeta has her stall just north of this spit. She haggles too hard, and the village is better for her anyway. Okeeh-Jas sells from hers, just south-south-west.
It is you, it is you! Did you see the boats come in? Huge, the big one, huge!
Who are you, big one? Where did you come from? What are you carrying? Is any of it shiny?

Leeks? Wild leeks grow just north-west of here, close by the fish barrels. I hate the fish barrels because they smell. Emperor Parasol Moss hangs a short way north, big one. I have not been told what it is for.
This is our village, big one. Look, a rowboat, drawn up just east-north-east of here. It is a huge boat. I am not going to ask you for a ride.
I am Peeks-Under-Boats. I look at everything, and I run errands. One day I will be a boat captain, big one. I practise on the frogs. They do not obey me yet.

Flaa Heet, the headman, is usually by the cooking spit, just south of here. He knows a great deal, big one. Hums-To-The-Rain is just south-south-west, on the west side of the village. Hums-To-The-Rain sings too much.

Soulrest, buyer? That is where the real coin is. Follow the shore north-east, a short way past the rowing boat, until the burnt-out house is on your right. Walk north-east a short way to the big ship, then follow the shore north-east a short way until Lilmoth Dock is on your right. From there climb south-east a fair way. Soulrest is there. Good trade.

Hereguard? Walk north-west a fair way until Lilmoth is on your right. Then follow the shore west a short way until you reach the dead tree on your right. Walk south-west a short way from the tree, and Hereguard Plantation is there.
Good trade comes back. Come closer and I will set aside the best of the day for you before anyone else sees it. Okeeh-Jas does not need to hear about it.
Buyer. You came in from the dock, so mine is the first stall you have met. Look here before you look anywhere else.
I am Tseeta. I sell the village's surplus to whoever walks in from the dock. I took the north side so that I meet buyers before Okeeh-Jas does.
Food and small goods, buyer. Show me your coin and I will name a price. Good trade.
Okeeh-Jas has the other stall, just south of mine. You can see it from here. Watch how she smiles when she names her price, buyer.
I sell what the village has left over, buyer: fish, roots and small goods. The fish is in the barrels just north-north-west of my stall, in sight, if you want to look before you buy.
Mm, I know your step. Sit by the nets with me, friend. The rope is dry enough for talking.
Mm. Traveller. Mind the nets. They are still wet.
Gourds grow a short way north-north-east of here, and so does a swamp fungal pod. Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow in one patch the same short way off. Mm, take only what is ripe, traveller.
I mend the nets on the west side, where they dry. The villagers keep a meat barrel out on the marsh, a short way north-north-west of here. Hm, I would sooner walk that way than inside Lilmoth.
Mm. An Argonian kept long from their own Hist fades. The colour thins and the markings go soft. They come back when the person goes home.
I am Hums-To-The-Rain. I mend the nets and gather what grows on the marsh. I came from a tribe inland years ago and that is all I say about it.
The rowing boat? It is just south of my stall. Look that way and there it is, so you cannot miss it.
The dock is north-east a fair way. You pass the rowing boat first and then the burnt-out house, and there is Lilmoth Dock.
Ah, look at you, not a scratch on you this time, you see? Come and sit by the stall and tell me everything, friend. I have been saving the news for you.
Well, you are new here, are you not? Tired walk, that. I can see it. Buy something or tell me where you have been.

Black Marsh, you ask, as if it were one thing, you see? What I know is that an owing can be sold on, so if a holder is owed months by a debtor, he can sell those months to a man who needs hands. The worker goes with them.
There is a drinker called Deep-In-His-Cups. He sits out on the shore track, a short way north-east of my stall, and he talks to anyone who stays a while. I think he knows more than he lets on.

I am Okeeh-Jas. This is my stall, south side, where the rowboat comes in. I married into this village and I still talk like the city, they tell me. I trade with anyone who lands. I like the gossip as much as the coin.
I sell food and small goods from this stall, and the fish is fresh, whatever you may have heard. Look all you like. I will laugh at my own prices with you.
Wet, customer? A short way east of our bedrolls there is a door that leads indoors. A fighter should get out of the rain.
Walking Dead, customer. They walk outside Lilmoth's walls, and there are some a short way north-north-west of our bedrolls. Keep your fists up.
Lilmoth Dock, customer? Follow the boards east, just until the burnt-out house is on your right. Then go north-east a short way, and you will see the dock.
Ha! Look who it is, my friend. Sit by the fire. I am glad of a face that I trust.
Well, customer. Got coin, or just questions?
I am Haxal-Tei. I fight with my fists and I fight for whoever pays the band. I talk the terms, so if you want a job done, you talk to me.
The band is camped here. Heem-Tsal, the fire mage, is just west-south-west of these bedrolls, and Keeps-Both-Edges is just west of him. I trust Keeps-Both-Edges with my purse.

You mean the Dwemer ruin, ojel. Walk north-east a short way until the big ship is on your left, then follow the shore south-east just until you reach the burnt-out house, also on your left. From there climb east over open ground a fair way until you reach Soulrest on your left, then climb east a short way more, and the ruin is there.
Ah, I am glad of you. Sit by me and ask whatever you like. I will answer it properly.
Yes, ojel? If you want something, say it plainly. I was reading.

An alchemist would find all three plants useful, ojel. Jazbay, lavender and juniper share a patch just north-west of here. I would sooner see them gathered by someone who knows the difference between them. Precisely.
You ask about Black Marsh. Ask Flaa Heet how Lilmoth is governed. I would have written it down myself, but the tree-minders of Lilmoth refused to let me sit by the city's Hist and take notes.
I am Heem-Tsal. I cast fire for this band and read whatever I can get my claws on. I travel with them for the passage south. I have not yet found a reason to leave.
If you want a book, ojel, try Hereguard Plantation, a fair way west of here. The bookseller Looks-At-Books keeps her shelf there. I have heard of that shelf, and I intend to see it.
The gravestones lie north of Lilmoth's walls, a short way north-west of here, and the dead have risen among them. A crocodile lies in the water a short way west. Keep clear of both.
You. Good. Stand by me a moment. The track is quiet. I would like it to stay so.
You there. What do you want? Keep your hands where I can see them.
Dead trees stand along the shore track just north-east of here. The band camps among them.
I carry a blade in each hand. I keep the band's watch. I was a guard once. I will not tell you for whom.
Two Argonians loiter by the leeks to the north. Sheeh-Vos stands just north-north-east of here, Waits-For-Lanterns just north-east. I do not trust either one.
Flaa Heet, is it? Walk south-west a short way, fellow, until you come to the rowing boat. Then follow the shore south-west another short way, and the village is there.
The dock? It is just north-north-east of here, fellow, in plain sight along the shore. I have watched it long enough to know.
Ahh, my friend, my friend. Sit down and tell me you brought something to wet the throat. I will tell you about the boat again, if you will have it.
Hm? Oh. What do you want, fellow? I am only sitting.
Black Marsh is wide. I have seen only the water of it. There is a big ship tied up at the dock now, with steps going down beside it to the water. I watched them load her, I did, every crate.
There are three dead Dunmer lying at the east end of Lilmoth Dock, a short way north-north-east of here, and they have not been buried. I do not go near, fellow, but I notice who does.
Deep-In-His-Cups, they call me. I earned it. I was a boatman once, and I lost my boat. Sit a while and I will tell you how, fellow.
Come close, friend. Keep your voice low, eh? I know you. The dock is quiet.
Hsst. Do not stand over me, cousin. I am only picking leeks.
Leeks grow all around me here, and more just west-south-west. Pick them slowly and look bored while you do it.
Past the bodies at the dock's east end there is a chest, a short way east-north-east of here. Look in it before anyone else does.
Dunmer lie just north-east of here, and they have not been searched. Whoever gets to their pockets first keeps what is in them, so go quietly.
I am Sheeh-Vos. I gather what the dock loses. I do not ask who owned it. Do not look at my hands for too long.
Deep-In-His-Cups sits just south-south-east of here. He sees everything at the dock and remembers half of it. He is a better source than I am.
The Walking Dead wander outside the city walls, honoured guest, a short way north-west of here. I would not hurry past them. A patient man keeps to the shadows and lets them go by.
Ah. You came back, my friend. Stand here beside me, where the shadows are good, and tell me what you have seen.
Honoured guest. You speak to me in plain sight, which I would not have chosen. Say what you want, slowly.
A hungry man can eat on this shore, honoured guest. Gourds grow along it, a short way west-south-west of here. Take what you need.
Below the walls there is a door, a short way west-north-west of here. It leads indoors and is well out of the way. I will say no more than that.
There is a thing I know. I do not give it to a stranger, honoured guest. Come back when I have had cause to trust you. Perhaps I will speak then.

Look to the graves north of the walls, a short way north-west of here. There is a trapdoor in the ground that leads down under the city. The chest beside it has already been emptied, so do not expect a reward.

I am Waits-For-Lanterns. I plan small jobs and I wait for dark to do them. It is a slow season, honoured guest, nothing more. I stand nearest the dock, where I can count the lanterns and the guards between them.
Easy water, traveller, but keep your eyes open to the south-south-east. A bear and her cubs roam a short way off that way, and a Tree Mother lives in the woods there too. Stay clear of both.
The Dwemer Ruin, traveller? Easy enough. Walk south-east from here a short way and you are standing in it.

Alten Merihall, traveller? Walk south-east a short way, until the Dwemer Ruin is on your left, and then keep south-east a fair way. Alten Merihall is there, and the money with it. There is a water route too, for those who prefer boats.
Lilmoth Dock, traveller? Walk west a short way, until the big ship is on your left, and then climb west a fair way. The dock is there.
Easy water, my friend! Sit by me a while. There is room on the landing. I chose Soulrest over Lilmoth Dock because there is no licence to be shown here. Now I have good company besides.
Easy water, traveller. This is Soulrest, and I run a boat from the landing here. Where are you going, and do you need a boat to get there?
Soulrest is where the boats tie up, traveller. Mine is one of them. A large ship lies west of here, a short way to the west-south-west, with a door aboard if you want to look inside.

Lilmoth fell, traveller. The outside traders went elsewhere after that. Alten Merihall's merchants have taken much of the bay's trade since then. That is where the money is now. I would carry you there gladly.

Heavy-Rope leads a crew on Soulrest's dock. The crew want their season ended early, traveller. The broker who hires them out will not hear of it. I only watch from the landing, so go and ask Heavy-Rope yourself.
I am Seeks-The-Channel, and I run a boat out of Soulrest, east of Lilmoth Dock. I wait here at the head of the landing between fares. I chose this place because no licence is asked for here.
You are back, my friend. Come to the stall. I will sell you what I have at last season's price, and not a coin more.
Outsider. Buy something or move along. Do not touch the goods.
Gourds grow just north-north-west of this stall. Pick your own. Mine are for sale.
This is Soulrest. Houses open onto it, one just south of me and another just south-east. Keep your hands off the doors, outsider.
I am Ushaa-Mei. I sell food here on the south-west side, between the houses. I remember what everything cost last season, so do not try to argue.
Food and small goods. I sell them at last season's price. I weigh it fair and I expect the coin to be good.
Plaits-The-Reed sits just west of me. I like her. Ask her yourself.
Hello again! Sit by the fire with me, and I will tell you what the grown-ups said today.
Hello, sir. Or miss. Please, do you smile?
Deathbell, nightshade, jazbay and other flowers grow together, miss. They are just south-east of here.
This is Soulrest, sir. Two cows graze just east-north-east of here, and Cow-Chaser scares them on purpose. Then he says it was me.
I am Little-Gecko. I sit in the middle, sir, where the grown-ups talk, so I hear everything. One day I will be a boat captain.
Seeks-The-Channel, the boat captain, stands just east of here. She is the best captain there is. Feldril Nethri, the Dunmer, works just north-east. He is kind to me, miss.
A Vale Deer lies dead just south-east of here, child. Something killed it. I would not go looking for the cause.
Child, you came back. Sit by me, out of the wind, and let me look at your hands. Tell me how you are.
Mind the reeds, child. I have not finished with them yet.
Glowing mushrooms and creep cluster grow under the trees, a short way south of here, child. I do not go that far now.
An Argonian kept long from the Hist grows pale, child. The colour thins and the markings go soft. When they go home, it all comes back.
Careful hands are sometimes of use to Tilts-The-Jug, child. Inside the house on Soulrest's dock, I am told. I always look at a stranger's hands first. Let me see yours.
I am Plaits-The-Reed. I weave mats and baskets for the families here, and for the boats. My husband is out fishing, child. He will be back soon.
Xeeh-Nah works just east-south-east of here. Xeeh-Nah should marry, I always say. Go and see, child.
Warrior! You are here! Did you bring the sword? Show me, show me, I will not touch it.
Hey, warrior! Have you got a sword? Do you have any scars? Show me one!
Gourds? They grow just north-west of here, warrior. I could carry them all myself, but I am busy with the cows.
This is Soulrest, and I am the best fighter in it! Ask the cows. A boar roots a short way north-east of here, and I am going to fight it one day.
I am Cow-Chaser, a hatchling of Soulrest, and I am going to be a warrior! I practise on the cows, because they run and that makes them hard to hit. Do you have a real sword?
Little-Gecko sits just west-south-west of here. Little-Gecko is a baby. Xeeh-Nah works just south of here. Xeeh-Nah is the strongest person alive! Go and see for yourself, warrior.

Go north-west a fair way, until Lilmoth Dock is on your left. Climb west a short way to the big ship on your left. Then west again, a short way, to the dead tree on your left. From there, ask again, ojel. The plantation lies further west.
Kin. Good. Sit by the benches a while. I will move the loads later.
Mm. What do you want, ojel? I have loads to move.
There is a chest by the big ship. It is a short way west-south-west of here. I do not know more than that.
On the big docks they hire a ship's crew with another man's months of owing. The harbourmaster calls it hiring. Free hands lose their paid work to it.
Tilts-The-Jug sometimes wants careful hands, ojel. Mine are for hauling. Try the house on the dock.
I am Xeeh-Nah. I haul cargo and tie up the boats here at Soulrest, on the south-east side. Half the people of Soulrest owe me money.
I carry loads and tie the boats up. The big ship lies a short way west of here. Its door leads aboard.
Ah, it is you. Few people trouble to cross to this end of the room. I do not forget the ones who do. Stay a while, friend.
Well, outlander. You have found the corner of Soulrest where visitors do not come by choice. State your business and I shall tell you whether I can oblige.

This is Soulrest, outlander. I am not permitted by the fire with the families, so I am put at this end. The north door is just west of me and another just east-south-east. The cooking pot stands just south-east, though I would not say I am welcome to it.

Here a debt is paid in work, outlander. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour that are counted in nushmeekos. When the months are worked the matter is over, so they say. Once, foreigners without a licence were kept to the docks at Lilmoth and barred from the city.

The crew that Heavy-Rope leads works Soulrest's dock, outlander. They want their season ended early. The broker who hires out their labour refuses. I was a trader once, and I know a broker's terms win over a man's wishes. Ask for Heavy-Rope there.

I am Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer. For now I am a guest of this marsh, though the hospitality has terms. I came to trade. I lost a cargo and was assessed months of labour. I cannot see when they will end, outlander.
There is a child called Little-Gecko, sitting just south-west of here. She is kind to me, which is more than I can say for most under this roof. I would thank you not to trouble her.

take: The first quest, A Dry Hand in a Wet City, was easy to follow. S'Tabi sent me to the boat captain, who sent me to fetch a necklace. I took it from an unlocked strongbox, returned it for 100 gold, and travelled to the Night-Reed Chapter. It was clear what to do at each step, and the go and marker commands made travel painless. Problems: nearly all dialogue was placeholder text ("not yet written; the gist"), so the characters had no voice and I learned little about who they were or why the Chapter matters. The boat captain was labelled "Argonian Boat Captain" even though she is Tilts-The-Jug, which confused me. The lockpicks were never needed because the box was unlocked. The theft felt too easy, and nobody reacted to me taking it in front of a crowd. Flaa Heet was also the person at the marker where I expected Bent-Spine. A new quest, The Drowned Lockbox, began right away. I am mildly curious about it, but I stopped at the end of the first quest.
answers: 1. Ask Bent-Spine what work he has for me, which starts The Drowned Lockbox. 2. The Night-Reed Chapter, a thieves guild. I am a Lookout, taken in after returning the necklace. I do not know their goals or what they want from me. 3. Flaa Heet appearing where Bent-Spine should be, and the boat captain being labelled that way when her name is Tilts-The-Jug. The placeholder dialogue was also confusing. 4. Write the real dialogue so the characters have personality and motives. Label NPCs by their real names. Make the lockpicks matter, and have the crowd react to theft.
